rv.q: Yes, this is a huge concert — not a full production.
Few musicals could sustain that kind of post-facto focus. Almost none, actually. But the sung-through 'Les Misérables' sure can.
It is dramatic, epic, and a glorious throwback to a time when budgets felt irrelevant.
By almost every measure, the concert lives up to the challenge, delivering both the promised spectacle and the heartfelt humanity at its core.
You couldn’t ask for a better way to hear this glorious score.
Most important, the concert sounds glorious.
Experiencing 'Les Mis' at Radio City is hugely overwhelming, much larger than life, whether you regard 'Les Miserables' as kitsch or as a classic.
Between a cast of vocal powerhouses and sound design that turns Radio City into a cathedral, it's easy to forgive the clunky visuals and just let the score of Les Misérables take over.

cn.t: Critics enthusiastically embrace this arena concert staging of the beloved musical, praising its spectacular production values and the enduring power of its iconic score, with some calling it nearly a religious theatrical experience.
